summary.oneLiner: The deck positions Amara Raja Energy & Mobility (formerly Amara Raja Batteries) as one of India's largest lead-acid battery makers with leading automotive and telecom/data-centre franchises, now redeploying its cash generation into an INR 95 Bn New Energy "Giga Corridor" in Telangana to lead India's energy transition.

hero.oneLiner: The deck positions Amara Raja Energy & Mobility (formerly Amara Raja Batteries) as one of India's largest lead-acid battery makers with leading automotive and telecom/data-centre franchises, now redeploying its cash generation into an INR 95 Bn New Energy "Giga Corridor" in Telangana to lead India's energy transition.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Described as "one of the largest manufacturers of lead-acid batteries in India", with brands 'Amaron', 'PowerZone' and 'Quanta'; the 2023 name change from Amara Raja Batteries Limited "reflects, the broader vision to lead India's Energy Transition, in the Energy & Mobility space by providing comprehensive energy solutions".
- Claims "Leading Automotive Battery Brand", "Largest Exporter of automotive Batteries" and "Strong Brand recall", exporting to 70+ countries; 4 decades of experience and ~12,000 employees.
- In industrial, claims "Pioneers in VRLA batteries in India", "Market Leader in Telecom sector/Largest exporter for VRLA batteries", "Largest Integrated Facility for MVRLA Batteries" and "Market Leader in Telecom and Data Centre Industry".
- Claims first-mover credentials: "First VRLA battery manufacturer", "First AGM battery manufacturer for 2W", and "Developed India's First 21700 Cylindrical Cell (NMC 811)".
- "Rank 1 in S&P Global ESG rating in respective sector in India"; AA+ credit rating by CRISIL; ~1/3rd of shares held by institutional shareholders.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- "Minimal debt in the books" - consolidated non-current borrowings were INR 260 Mn in FY24 and nil in FY25 and FY26; current borrowings INR 273 Mn (FY24), 1,446 Mn (FY25), 2,765 Mn (FY26); AA+ credit rating by CRISIL.
- Returns: "~12% ROCE" as on FY26 end at consolidated level; consolidated ROCE 19.2% (FY24), 16.2% (FY25), 12.0% (FY26) and ROE 14.6%/13.3%/11.6%, with the deck noting "ROCE excluding long term investments is ~12.5% for FY26" consolidated and "~18.3% for FY26" standalone.
- Reinvestment is the visible use of capital: consolidated Capital Work-in-Progress rose from INR 6,255 Mn (FY24) to 12,975 Mn (FY25) to 15,847 Mn (FY26), and PP&E from 29,095 Mn to 37,695 Mn over the same period, funded alongside networth growing from 67,987 Mn (FY24) to 80,990 Mn (FY26).
- New Energy capital is routed through wholly owned subsidiary ARACT (Rs. 1,900 crore infused till date) against the INR 95 Bn Giga Corridor plan.
- Shareholding as on 30th June 2026: Promoter 32.86%, FIIs 17.34%, DIIs 15.30%, Public 34.50%; market cap ~INR 154 Bn+ as on Jun 30, 2026 and shares outstanding 183.0 Mn.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Rename] Renamed from Amara Raja Batteries Limited to Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Limited in 2023 to signal the shift beyond lead-acid batteries.
- [Group structure] Two named wholly owned subsidiaries carry the strategic build-out: ARACT (Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies) for cells and the 10 GWh BESS plant, and ARCSPL for the lead recycling facility that commenced operations in FY25.
- [Insurance/plant incident] Exceptional income in FY25 of INR 1,111 Mn and in FY26 (net) including INR 1,218 Mn and INR 1,812 Mn relates to insurance claims on the TBD/tubular plant - indicating a plant loss event being recovered through insurance rather than operating performance.
- [Regulation] An INR 476 Mn exceptional expense in Q3 FY26 is attributed to a "change in Labour Code".
- [Distribution] Automotive domestic network slide lists 17, 1,00,000+, 40 and 1500+ against Branches, Distribution Points, Direct Partners and Points of Sale, but the label-to-value binding is not recoverable from this extraction, so the individual counts are not asserted here.
